children: recent acquisition of a 50% stake in Sandals Resorts presents "substantial" synergies for the company and represents a transaction that could vault Royal Caribbean ahead of cruise peers, says Citi Research analyst James Hardiman, who put Buy-rated Royal Caribbean on a 90-day positive Catalyst Watch.
it invested ~$3B for a 50% stake in Sandals and Beaches, implying a total enterprise value of ~$6B.
The acquisition and talking points surrounding the deal suggest a straightforward move into the all-inclusive resort business, a distinction that transforms Royal Caribbean
from a pure play cruise operator into “something much broader” through its land destinations, river cruising, and what management refers to as a “lifetime of vacations” strategy.

“If, and when, the vacation choice becomes less about one ship vs. another and more about one vacation ecosystem vs. another, this choice becomes more obvious as RCL builds out a portfolio the breadth of which dwarfs the competition,” Hardiman writes in his note.

Post-announcement, management seemed to focus on what RCL can do for the resorts, repeatedly emphasizing that Sandals is already a high-quality asset with attractive margins, strong customer loyalty, meaningful brand awareness, and substantial development opportunities.
But Hardiman believes a more important question is what can Sandals do for RCL? Layering Sandals and Beaches on top of Royal Caribbean’s

land destinations (Perfect Day CocoCay, Royal Beach Club Nassau, Royal Beach Club Cozumel, etc.) “Increasingly creates a Caribbean ecosystem that does not exist elsewhere in the cruise industry and has not existed in the history of the travel industry.”
More importantly, Hardiman believes this transaction has the potential to widen the competitive gap between RCL and the rest of the cruise industry.

“Over time, RCL could increasingly compete with an ecosystem that includes ships, resorts, beach clubs, private destinations, river cruises, and a unified loyalty platform tying everything together,” Hardiman says.
After retreating to a 16-month low of $222.22 on Wednesday, shares of Royal Caribbean
are up close to 5%, outperforming much more modest gains for rivals Carnival Corp.

title: Royal Caribbean's Sandals play earns a 90-day positive catalyst watch—Citi Research
